assertion.statement: For the actual signed unit-filter parameters, each newly ramified prime outside S contributes (-1/p), and their product is fixed by the sign and dyadic unit class.
assertion.objects: The fixed curve E of the nonvanishing section, S containing2,3 and all bad primes, and odd signed squarefree t coprime to S.
assertion.hypotheses: The parameter has the prescribed real sign and local unit squareclasses; E is good outside S.
assertion.quantifiers: Every parameter in this fixed signed unit filter.
assertion.parameter_range: New primes p|t outside S, necessarily p>=5.
assertion.uniformity: The product of the new factors is constant over the filter; no nonvanishing uniformity follows.
assertion.constants: Exact signs only; no analytic constants.
assertion.normalizations: Quadratic twist by t, not by an incorrectly assumed odd fundamental discriminant; D_p inversion does not change ±1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: At2,3 and old bad primes use local isomorphism from equal squareclasses. Classes3 or7 modulo8 remain allowed; discriminant may be4t.
assertion.limit_order: Fix S and the signed unit filter, then choose a parameter; compute local factors and their finite product.

available_assertion.statement: For p>=5, p|t with t nonzero squarefree, and E of good reduction type I0, W_p(E_t)=(-1/p).
available_assertion.objects: An elliptic curve E/Q_p, its quadratic twist E_t, and local root numbers in {±1}.
available_assertion.hypotheses: p>=5; squarefree nonzero integer t; p divides t; E has good reduction.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Only the type I0 branch of Proposition3.3(2).
available_assertion.uniformity: Independent of unit part of t in this branch.
available_assertion.constants: The value is exactly the Legendre symbol (-1/p).
available_assertion.normalizations: Desjardins defines W_p(E)=D_p W_p(E_t); D_p²=1 and good reduction gives W_p(E)=1.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No p2 or p3 conclusion is asserted; other reduction types are not consumed.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix E and a squarefree parameter t, then apply at its prime divisors p>=5.
